h1:
Krabi Desserts, Sweets & Cafés
11 Spots the Locals Actually Go
intro: Krabi isn't just beaches and seafood. The sweets here run from southern Thai classics like tao sor and Lanta sand cookies, rooted in the local Hokkien-Chinese community, all the way to fresh-coconut bua loy shops and a new wave of cafés with mountain and river views. We've pulled together the in-town dessert shops where you can actually sit and eat, plus the cafés worth driving to around the edge of the city, each with its neighborhood and a rough price from what we found.

blocks.html: Krabi desserts split roughly into three lanes. The first is the in-town cold-sweet shops — fresh-coconut bua loy, grass jelly with Thai tea, salted-yolk ice cream — the kind of thing you grab to cool off after walking around. The second is the southern Thai sweets you can take home as gifts, like tao sor and Lanta sand cookies. The third is the newer cafés around the edge of town that are really about the setting plus a cake or some baking. We've put all three in one list, starting with the in-town dessert shops, then heading out to the cafés on the outskirts.

items.name: KAINOM
items.blurb: A small dessert shop in central Krabi and one of the most talked-about in reviews. The draws are fresh-coconut bua loy, coconut sago, salted-yolk ice cream and grass jelly with Thai tea, all piled with toppings. It's halal, you can sit and eat in, and it's a good afternoon stop to cool down.

items.name: Bua Loy by Jongjaroen, Krabi branch
items.blurb: A well-known bua loy brand from Hat Yai that opened a Krabi branch. The selling point is sweet-egg bua loy and black-sesame bua loy with rich fresh coconut milk, with Thai tea and salted-yolk ice cream to order alongside. The shop is new and clean, and it suits anyone who likes their sweets properly sweet.

items.name: Sweet & Sour ice cream & dessert cafe
items.blurb: A dessert café split into several zones with plenty of photo corners. The main thing is ice cream in lots of styles, plus desserts and coffee. Good for a group of friends who want to linger and take photos. Open Tuesday–Sunday, 10:30–18:00.
items.meta: Krabi town · ice cream café · closed Mondays

items.name: Old-style purple-yam dumplings (Ruean Thip)
items.blurb: An old-school sweet that locals in Krabi recommend — thin pastry, a generous filling, gentle purple yam that's sweet but not cloying. Buy it to snack on or carry home. It's getting harder to find these days, so if you spot it, give it a try.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: A lot of the in-town cold-sweet shops are small and open only for part of the day — some start in the afternoon and sell out before evening. If you've got a particular one in mind, check the opening hours on its page before heading over to be safe, and note that many take cash only.

If you want sweets that really carry the local culture, Krabi has traditional ones that clearly reflect its Hokkien-Chinese community and southern Thai way of life. The two to know are tao sor and Lanta sand cookies. They're mostly sold as gifts, but they're easy to unwrap and eat on the road too.

items: Tao sor — a sweet that looks a lot like a Chinese-style mung-bean pastry (khanom pia), with both a sweet filling and a savory one studded with salted egg yolk. It's a legacy of the southern Hokkien-Chinese community. Several well-known shops in town sell it, such as Jee-Or and Pornthip.

Lanta sand cookies (khanom sai / khanom khi mod) — a specialty from Koh Lanta that's become a province-wide gift. The texture is crumbly like sand, made from coconut, rice flour, salt and sugar — sweet, fragrant and rich. It goes well with black coffee.
Krabi cake — a dense gift-style cake that Krabi's gift shops bake and sell. It keeps for a while and travels easily as carry-on.

Traditional Thai sweets — around the Ao Nang night market and the in-town markets you'll find a rotating set of homestyle Thai sweets, like khanom chan, khanom tom and khanom kluai, priced in the tens of baht.

blocks.title: One-stop gift shopping
blocks.html: If you're short on time, just stop by a big gift shop like Jee-Or — it pulls together tao sor, Krabi cake and a range of local sweets in one place. But if you want fresher items at friendlier prices, walk the in-town market in the morning, where you'll find the regular stalls the locals buy from.

blocks.text: Cafés worth a sit around Krabi

blocks.html: Krabi's newer cafés are mostly about the setting. There are minimalist spots in town that lean on their baking, and out-of-town cafés selling mountain, river and sea views. Pick based on the rhythm of your trip — if you're in town in the morning, drop into a bakery café; if you've got a car and want to settle in, drive out to a view café on the edge of the city.

items.name: Much Mellow
items.blurb: A minimalist, wood-toned café in Soi Maharaj 2 in central Krabi, known for its signature croissants and homemade baking. There are fusion dishes and vegan options too. Good for a late breakfast or a coffee while you work in town.

items.name: EP's Cafe Patisserie
items.blurb: A polished-looking café in town with a fairly complete bakery — cakes, pastries, food and drinks. Service is good, and the prices aren't as high as the room makes you expect. Good for anyone who likes sitting in a smart-looking spot in town.

items.name: BE TREE CAFE
items.blurb: A white, minimalist café on the Sai Thai side, on the road between town and Ao Nang, about 7 km out of the city. It has food, drinks and baking — a good rest stop if you're driving toward Ao Nang. Opens around 09:00.

items.name: Into the Forest
items.blurb: A café-restaurant tucked into shady greenery. The menu is broad — steak, pasta, salads, croissants and cake — so it works as a real meal plus dessert. If you like a quiet, woodsy setting, this one will land.

items.name: Baan Ton Mai Cafe
items.blurb: A riverside café wrapped in trees, with several seating zones to choose from. Good for settling in to catch the breeze — order a coffee and a dessert and just chill. Open daily, roughly 09:00–18:00.

items.name: Khaothong Hill
items.blurb: A hilltop café in the Khao Thong area with long views over Krabi's sea and mangrove forest. It has food, drinks and baking. Go in the late afternoon to catch the sunset. Open daily, roughly 11:00–20:00.

items.name: Traditional Thai Sweets by Asiyah
items.blurb: A stall-shop of homestyle Thai sweets in the Ao Nang night market, with fresh-made sweets that rotate by the day at friendly prices. Good to grab as you walk the evening market around Ao Nang.
items.meta: Ao Nang night market · homestyle Thai sweets

blocks.text: Plan a full day of sweets and cafés

blocks.html: If you want to make the most of Krabi's sweets and cafés in a single day, here's an easy route. Start in town in the morning and around midday, then move out of the city in the afternoon and evening to catch the views.

blocks.label: In-town café route
blocks.title: A half day that works even without a car

items.activity: Start at Much Mellow or EP's Cafe Patisserie
items.note: Late breakfast + coffee + croissant/cake, walkable in town

items.activity: Stop by a cold-sweet shop — KAINOM or Bua Loy by Jongjaroen
items.note: Cool off with fresh-coconut bua loy / salted-yolk ice cream

items.activity: Walk the in-town market for gifts
items.note: Carry home tao sor, Lanta sand cookies, Krabi cake

blocks.label: View-café route
blocks.title: A half day with a car, out of town for the views

items.activity: Drive toward Ao Nang, stop at BE TREE CAFE in Sai Thai
items.note: A bakery break before you reach the sea

items.activity: Settle in at Baan Ton Mai Cafe or Into the Forest
items.note: Riverside / garden — order a dessert and a coffee

items.activity: Finish at Khaothong Hill for the sunset
items.note: Arrive before evening for the best spot; busy on weekends

faq.q: What local Krabi sweets should I try?
faq.a: The standouts are tao sor — a pastry that looks like a Chinese-style mung-bean cake (khanom pia) and comes from the Hokkien-Chinese community — and Lanta sand cookies (khanom khi mod), which are crumbly, sweet and rich. Both are province-wide gifts. On the cold-sweet side, look for fresh-coconut bua loy and salted-yolk ice cream at the in-town dessert shops.

faq.q: Which sit-down dessert shop in Krabi town is best?
faq.a: KAINOM gets a lot of mentions in reviews, with fresh-coconut bua loy and salted-yolk ice cream as the highlights, and it's halal. Another is Bua Loy by Jongjaroen, Krabi branch, a well-known Hat Yai brand that opened here. Both are in town and you can sit and eat in.

faq.q: Where are the Krabi cafés with good views?
faq.a: For views you'll need to head out of town. Khaothong Hill sits on a hill in the Khao Thong area with views over the sea and mangrove forest — good in the late afternoon. Baan Ton Mai Cafe and Into the Forest lean on a riverside and garden setting, good for settling in for a while.

faq.q: Where's the easiest place to buy Krabi sweets as gifts?
faq.a: If you want it all in one place, stop by a big gift shop like Jee-Or, which gathers tao sor, Krabi cake and a range of local sweets. But if you want fresher items at lower prices, walk the in-town market in the morning and find the regular stalls.

faq.q: Do Krabi dessert shops take cards / PromptPay?
faq.a: Most of the bigger cafés in town take bank transfer / PromptPay, but plenty of the small dessert shops and market stalls still lean on cash. Keeping some cash on you is the easiest way to go.
